title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The oak wood of Corpes: the daughters stripped, beaten and abandoned (tiradas 128–130, lines 2675–2762)
part: Tiradas 128–130 · The oak wood of Corpes: the daughters stripped, beaten and abandoned (lines 2675–2762)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 295–300, lines 2675–2762 (tiradas 128–130). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.t:
“¿Dezidme, qué vos fiz, ifantes de Carrión!
yo sirviéndovos sin art, e vos conssejastes mi[e] mu[o]rt.
sentences.l:
“Tell-me, what to-you I-did, Infantes of Carrión!
I serving-you without guile, and you plotted my death.
sentences.i: “Tell me, Infantes of Carrión, what have I done to you? I served you without guile, and you plotted my death.
sentences.n: Tirada 128 (assonance ó / ó-e) — the Moor turns back to Molina, foreseeing the misfortune of the Çid's daughters; the travellers enter the kingdom of Castile; they sleep in the oak wood of Corpes; in the morning the Infantes are left alone with their wives and make ready to ill-treat them; Doña Sol's pleas are in vain; the cruelty of the Infantes (Pidal: El moro se torna a Molina, presintiendo la desgracia de las hijas del Cid. — Los viajeros entran en el reino de Castilla. — Duermen en el robledo de Corpes. — A la mañana quédanse solos los infantes con sus mujeres y se preparan a maltratarlas. — Ruegos inútiles de doña Sol. — Crueldad de los infantes). The line-ends run Carrión, mu[o]rt, traydores, Sol, señor …, Corpes, nu[ov]es, montes, pelliçones: stressed ó, often with an e after it. Avengalvón the Moor is still speaking: his speech began at v. 2677 in tirada 127 (the previous part). Pidal has moved these two lines: in the manuscript they stand after v. 2674, and he sets them here, keeping their numbers, at the head of the ó tirada whose assonance they share; so the count runs 2675, 2676, then 2681. Pidal opens the line with ” (his mark for a speech running on); here it takes an opening “, as this part's first line. The mixed marks ¿ … ! are his. Dezidme, imperative + me, 'tell me'. fiz, 'I did', the strong preterite 1st sg. of fer (fazer, f- for modern h-; = hice). yo sirviéndovos, a loose gerund clause, 'I serving you, while I served you'; vos is enclitic. sin art, 'without trickery' (art, 'trick, stratagem'). conssejastes, 2nd pl. preterite, 'you took counsel on, plotted' (= aconsejasteis): the Infantes' plan to kill him for his wealth (tirada 127). mi[e] mu[o]rt = mi muerte, 'my death': mie is the old feminine possessive, its e Pidal's, and in mu[o]rt the o is his, the old diphthong uo; mu[o]rt also gives the line its ó.

sentences.i: Here I part from you, as from wicked men and traitors. With your leave I will go, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol; I set little store by the good name of these men of Carrión.
sentences.n: Aquim = aquí + me, 'here I …' (parto me, 'I take my leave'). commo de malos e de traydores, 'as from wicked men and traitors'. Iré, future of ir. con vuestra graçia, 'with your leave', turning now to the two ladies; don Elvira as printed, Doña Elvira in the English. Pidal's note to v. 2683: 'nuevas, "renombre", v. 2084' — nuevas here is 'renown, reputation', not 'news'. poco preçio, 'I value little'. los de Carrión, 'those of Carrión', the Infantes.

sentences.t:
Dios lo quiera e lo mande, que de tod el mundo es señor,
d' aqueste casamiento que[s] grade el Campeador.”
sentences.l:
God it may-will and it may-command, who of all the world is lord,
of this marriage that-[himself] may-be-glad the Campeador.”
sentences.i: May God, who is lord of all the world, so will it and so ordain that the Campeador may have joy of this marriage.”
sentences.n: quiera … mande, present subjunctives of wish, 'may God will it and command it'. tod = todo, the final vowel dropped (apocope). The second line hangs on gradarse de, 'to be glad of, satisfied with' (as Grádanse, 'they rejoice', v. 172): que[s] grade = que se grade, present subjunctive, 'that he may be glad', the s Pidal's; d' aqueste casamiento, 'of this marriage', put first. The wish is a dark one: the rubric has the Moor foreseeing the daughters' misfortune. The speech ends here.

sentences.i: This he said to them, and the Moor turned back; he went playing at arms as he crossed the Jalón, and, like the man of good sense he was, went home to Molina.
sentences.n: ha dicho, 'he has said', the perfect beside the preterite tornó. se tornó, 'turned back' (twice, rhyming on itself). Pidal's note to v. 2687: '"iba jugando las armas al pasar el río Jalón". Por esta parte, frente a Medinaceli, el Jalón tiene todavía muy poco fondo y se pasa sin necesidad de vado' — 'he went playing at arms as he crossed the river Jalón. Hereabouts, opposite Medinaceli, the Jalón is still very shallow and can be crossed without needing a ford': teniendo iva armas, the display of horsemanship he made at v. 2673. troçir, 'to cross' (cf. v. 2653). Salón, the Jalón. qu[o]mmo = commo, 'as, like', the o Pidal's; de buen seso, 'of good sense'.

sentences.t:
Ya movieron del Anssarera ifantes de Carrión,
acójense a andar de día e de noch;
sentences.l:
Now they-moved from-the Anssarera, Infantes of Carrión,
they-take-themselves to travel by day and by night;
sentences.i: Now the Infantes of Carrión set out from the Ansarera, and took to the road by day and by night;
sentences.n: movieron, 'they set out' (mover, intransitive), preterite, then acójense, present: the epic mixing of tenses. del Anssarera, 'from the Ansarera', the place where they lodged in the previous part; del as printed. acójense = se acogen, 'they betake themselves, set themselves' (a andar, 'to travelling'). noch = noche, apocope.

sentences.i: on their left they leave Atienza, a mighty crag; the sierra of Miedes they crossed next, and through the Montes Claros they ride hard with the spur;
sentences.n: a ssiniestro, 'on the left' (ss as printed). Ati[en]ça = Atienza, the en Pidal's (the extent of his italics here was judged on the image and is not quite certain). una peña muy fu[o]rt, 'a very strong crag', the town on its rock; fu[o]rt = fuerte, the o Pidal's. Pidal's note to v. 2692: 'Sobre Miedes y Atienza, v. 415' — at v. 415 the exiled Çid camped at the sierra of Miedes on the right hand of Atienza; the Infantes now cross the same country going the other way, so that Atienza, on the Çid's right then, is on their left now. passáronla, 'they crossed it', the la taking up la sierra. estoz, 'then' (= entonces). Pidal's note to v. 2693: 'Montes Claros es hoy el rincón de la provincia de Guadalajara donde nace el río Jarama. Para que convenga al pasaje de nuestro Cantar que anotamos, este nombre debía extenderse por el Norte, dentro de la limítrofe provincia de Soria hacia Caracena' — 'Montes Claros is today the corner of the province of Guadalajara where the river Jarama rises. To fit this passage, the name must have reached north into the neighbouring province of Soria, towards Caracena.' aguijan a espolón, 'they spur on, hard with the spur'.

sentences.i: on their left they leave Griza, which Álamos founded — there are the caves where he shut Elpha up; on their right they leave San Esteban, but it lies far off.
sentences.n: assiniestro, a siniestro run together as printed, 'on the left'. Griza, Álamos and Elpha have no note from Pidal on these pages: a place and a local story the poem takes as known, and not otherwise explained here. pobló, 'settled, peopled'. caños is taken as 'caves, underground passages'; that Álamos is the one who shut Elpha up (a Elpha, the personal a before the object) is the simplest reading, not a certain one. a diestro, 'on the right'. aSant Estevan, a + Sant run together as printed: San Esteban de Gormaz on the Duero (Pidal, note to v. 2697). ca[d]e = cae, 'falls, lies', the d Pidal's; alu[o]n, 'far away', the o his. The tense slips again, from passáronla to dexan.

sentences.t:
Entrados son los ifantes al robredo de Corpes,
los montes son altos las ramas pujan con las nu[ov]es,
elas bestias fieras que andan aderredor.
sentences.l:
Entered are the Infantes into-the oak-wood of Corpes,
the woods are high, the branches rise with the clouds,
and-the beasts wild that go around.
sentences.i: The Infantes have come into the oak wood of Corpes: the woods are high, the branches climb to the clouds, and wild beasts roam all about.
sentences.n: Entrados son, 'they have entered': ser + past participle with a verb of motion. robredo = robledo, 'oak wood'. Pidal's note to v. 2697: 'El robredo de Corpes ha desaparecido hoy (v. página 88): existió al Suroeste de San Esteban de Gormaz, que es el Sant Estevan nombrado en el verso anterior' — 'the oak wood of Corpes has disappeared today (see p. 88); it lay south-west of San Esteban de Gormaz, the Sant Estevan named in the line before.' montes, 'wooded heights, forest', rather than 'mountains'. Pidal's note to v. 2698: 'pujan con las nuoves, "suben hasta las nubes"' — 'they rise up to the clouds'. nu[ov]es = nubes, the ov Pidal's (the italic extent read at high zoom, not certain). elas = e las, 'and the'; the line has no verb of its own: 'and the wild beasts that roam about (are there)'.

sentences.i: They came upon a green garden with a clear spring; the Infantes of Carrión have the tent pitched, and there they lie that night with all the people they have with them;
sentences.n: Fallaron = hallaron, 'they found' (f- for h-). vergel, 'garden, orchard', a green and pleasant spot. linpia fu[o]nt, 'clear spring', fuente with the o Pidal's. mandan fincar, 'they order to be set up' (fincar, 'to fix, set up'). con quantos que ellos traen, 'with as many as they bring'. i yazen, 'there they lie' (i = allí; yazer = yacer).

sentences.t:
con sus mugieres en braços demuéstranles amor;
¡mal gelo cunplieron quando salie el sol!
sentences.l:
with their wives in arms they-show-them love;
ill it-to-them they-fulfilled when came-out the sun!
sentences.i: with their wives in their arms they show them love — and ill they made it good to them when the sun came up!
sentences.n: demuéstranles = les demuestran, 'they show them'. Pidal's note to v. 2703: 'Aunque las hijas del Cid, según el pensamiento del poeta, eran de poca edad al desposarse (v. 2083), su casamiento es un matrimonio perfecto' — 'Though the Çid's daughters, as the poet conceives it, were young when betrothed, their marriage is a marriage in full'; he cites mugieres a bendiciones (2562, 2581) and parejas pora en braços (2761), and rejects the view that the marriage was never consummated. mal gelo cunplieron, 'badly they fulfilled it to them', the love of the night: gelo = ge + lo, 'it to them' (ge, ancestor of se). salie = salía, imperfect beside the preterite.

sentences.t:
Mandaron cargar las azémilas con averes [a nombre],
cogida han la tienda do albergaron de noch,
adelant eran idos los de criazón:
sentences.l:
They-ordered to-load the pack-mules with goods [in great number],
gathered they-have the tent where they-lodged by night,
ahead were gone those of household:
sentences.i: They had the pack mules loaded with riches in plenty and struck the tent where they had passed the night; their household folk had gone on ahead:
sentences.n: averes, 'goods, wealth'. [a nombre], both words Pidal's (in italics), restored to fill the line; Pidal gives no note, and 'in great number, in plenty' is the reading taken here, not a certain one. cogida han la tienda, 'they have taken down the tent', the participle agreeing with its object. albergaron, 'they lodged'. eran idos, 'they had gone' (ser as the auxiliary of a verb of motion). Pidal's note to v. 2707: 'los de criazón, sus familiares, las personas criadas en su casa' — 'their household, the people brought up in their house'.

sentences.t:
assí lo mandaron ifantes de Carrión,
que non i fincás ninguno, mugier nin varón,
si non amas sus mugieres doña Elvira e doña Sol:
deportar se quieren con ellas a todo su sabor.
sentences.l:
thus it ordered Infantes of Carrión,
that not there should-remain anyone, woman nor man,
except both their wives doña Elvira and doña Sol:
to-sport themselves they-wish with them at all their pleasure.
sentences.i: so the Infantes of Carrión had ordered, that none should stay behind, woman or man, save only their two wives, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol: they mean to take their sport with them as they please.
sentences.n: fincás = fincasse, imperfect subjunctive, the final -e dropped, 'that (no one) should remain'. non … ninguno, the double negative. si non, 'except'. amas = ambas, 'both'. Pidal's note to v. 2711: 'deportarse, "solazarse", "holgarse"' — 'to take one's ease, amuse oneself'; deportar se quieren, the se split from its verb, 'they want to amuse themselves'. a todo su sabor, 'entirely at their pleasure': what the pleasure is, the next lines say.

sentences.t:
Todos eran idos, ellos quatro solos son,
tanto mal comidieron ifantes de Carrión:
sentences.l:
All were gone, they four alone are,
so-much evil they-pondered Infantes of Carrión:
sentences.i: All the others had gone; the four of them are alone. Such harm had the Infantes of Carrión been brooding on:
sentences.n: eran idos, 'had gone'. ellos quatro solos son, 'the four of them are alone', the two Infantes and their wives. Pidal's note to v. 2713: 'comidieron, "meditaron"' — 'they pondered, plotted'.

sentences.t:
“Bien lo creades don Elvira e doña Sol,
aquí seredes escarnidas en estos fieros montes.
Oy nos partiremos, e daxadas seredes de nos;
non abredes part en tierras de Carrión.
sentences.l:
“Well it may-you-believe, don Elvira and doña Sol,
here you-will-be mocked in these wild woods.
Today we-will-part, and left you-will-be by us;
not you-will-have share in lands of Carrión.
sentences.i: “You may be sure of it, Doña Elvira and Doña Sol: here in these wild woods you will be put to shame. Today we part, and you will be left behind by us; you shall have no share in the lands of Carrión.
sentences.n: The Infantes speak together. Bien lo creades, 'well may you believe it', creades = creáis, present subjunctive; no comma after creades, as printed. seredes = seréis, future of ser. escarnidas, 'mocked, dishonoured' (escarnir; cf. escarnio). fieros montes, 'wild woods'. daxadas, so printed (= dexadas), 'left'. de nos, 'by us'. abredes = habréis, 'you will have'. part = parte, apocope: no share in the Carrión lands promised them as wives (the arras, the marriage settlement, of vv. 2564 and 2570).

sentences.t:
Irán aquestos mandados al Çid Campeador;
nos vengaremos aquesta por la del león.”
sentences.l:
Will-go these tidings to-the Çid Campeador;
we will-avenge this-one for the-one of-the lion.”
sentences.i: This news will go to the Çid Campeador: with this we shall have our revenge for the business of the lion.”
sentences.n: Irán, 'will go'. aquestos mandados, 'these tidings'. aquesta … la del león, feminine pronouns standing for a noun left unsaid (the thing, the shame: compare la desondra del león, v. 2762): 'we will avenge this one for the one of the lion', i.e. by this they pay back the shame they suffered when the Çid's lion got loose (vv. 2280 ff.). The speech ends here.

sentences.t:
Allí les tuellen los mantos e los pelliçones,
páranlas en cuerpos y en camisas y en çiclatones.
sentences.l:
There from-them they-take the mantles and the fur-robes,
they-set-them in bodies and in shifts and in ciclatons.
sentences.i: There they strip them of their mantles and fur robes and leave them with nothing but what clings to the body, their shifts and silken tunics.
sentences.n: tuellen, present of toller, 'they take away'. Pidal's note to v. 2720: 'pelliçones, v. p. 123' — fur robes, explained on that page of his introduction. Pidal's note to v. 2721: 'páranlas en cuerpos, "las dejan a cuerpo", con sola la ropa que ciñe el cuerpo, es decir, con sólo la camisa y el brial o ciclatón, v. 2750' — 'they leave them "in body", in only the clothing that fits close to the body, that is, the shift and the brial or ciclatón'. páranlas = las paran, 'they set them, leave them'. çiclatones, robes of rich silk cloth. The line-ends pelliçones, çiclatones keep the ó-e.

sentences.t:
Espuelas tienen calçadas los malos traydores,
en mano prenden las çinchas fuertes e duradores.
sentences.l:
Spurs they-have donned the wicked traitors,
in hand they-take the girths strong and lasting.
sentences.i: The wicked traitors have their spurs on their heels, and in their hands they take the saddle-girths, strong and tough.
sentences.n: Espuelas tienen calçadas, 'they have spurs put on', the participle agreeing with espuelas (calçar, 'to put on footwear or spurs'). prenden = toman, 'they take'. çinchas, 'girths', the broad straps that hold the saddle on the horse. duradores, 'lasting', here 'tough': an adjective in -dor, one form for both genders, here with feminine çinchas (as tajadores with espadas, v. 2726); its plural -ores gives the line its ó-e.

sentences.t:
Quando esto vieron las dueñas, fablava doña Sol:
“Por Dios vos rogamos, don Dí[a]go e don Ferrando, [nos]!
sentences.l:
When this saw the ladies, spoke doña Sol:
“By God you we-beg, don Dí[a]go and don Ferrando, [we]!
sentences.i: When the ladies saw this, Doña Sol spoke: “By God we beg you, Don Diego and Don Fernando — we beg you!
sentences.n: fablava, imperfect, 'spoke' (f- for h-), among presents and preterites. Doña Sol speaks for both. rogamos, 'we beg'. don Dí[a]go, the a Pidal's: Diego, as Ferrando is Fernando. [nos], 'we', the word Pidal's restoration: a pronoun added at the end to take up the subject of rogamos, giving the line its ó (compare mártires seremos nos, v. 2728, and prendemos nos, v. 2730). The line ends nos! with no opening ¡, as printed.

sentences.t:
dos espadas tenedes fuertes e tajadores,
al una dizen Colada e al otra Tizón,
cortandos las cabeças, mártires seremos nos.
sentences.l:
two swords you-have strong and cutting,
to-the one they-call Colada and to-the other Tizón,
cut-us the heads, martyrs we-will-be we.
sentences.i: you have two swords, strong and keen-edged — one they call Colada, the other Tizón: cut off our heads, and we shall be martyrs.
sentences.n: tenedes = tenéis. tajadores, 'cutting, keen' (tajar, 'to cut'). al una dizen Colada e al otra Tizón, 'to the one they say Colada and to the other Tizón': the Çid's swords, his parting gift to the Infantes (v. 2575). cortandos = cortadnos, imperative + nos with the d and n changing places, 'cut off our heads', as dándoslas = dadnos las at v. 2081 and indos = idnos at v. 832; Pidal gives no note here. A gerund (cortándonos) would need the nos whole, so the imperative is taken, after vos rogamos. mártires seremos nos, 'martyrs we shall be': better a death by the sword than the shame of a beating.

sentences.t:
Moros e cristianos departirán desta razón,
que por lo que nos mereçemos no lo prendemos nos.
sentences.l:
Moors and Christians will-talk of-this matter,
that for what we deserve not it we-take we.
sentences.i: Moors and Christians will talk of this, for it is not for anything we have deserved that we suffer it.
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 2729: 'Todo el mundo (comp. 145) hablará de esto', 'lo censurará' — 'all the world will speak of this, will condemn it': Moros e cristianos, everyone. departirán, future of departir, 'to discuss, talk over'. desta = de esta. razón, 'matter'. que por lo que nos mereçemos no lo prendemos nos, 'that it is not for what we deserve that we receive it'; no, so printed.

sentences.i: Do not work such wicked deeds upon us: if we are beaten, it is yourselves you will dishonour; you will be called to answer for it at a meeting or before the court.”
sentences.n: Atan = tan. Pidal's note to v. 2731: 'enssienplo, "hecho notable, acción"' — 'a notable deed, an act'. non fagades, present subjunctive as a prohibition, 'do not do'. Pidal's note to v. 2732: 'si nosotras fuéramos azotadas os envileceréis a vosotros mismos' — 'if we were beaten you will debase yourselves'. fuéremos, future subjunctive; majadas, 'beaten' (majar, 'to pound'). abiltaredes, future of abiltar, 'to debase, disgrace'. Pidal's note to v. 2733: '"os lo demandarán en vistas o cortes". Las vistas, o entrevistas convenidas de antemano, a veces tenían carácter judicial, como las juntas o asambleas judiciales de distrito que se mencionan en 2014, 2949; éstas, aunque a veces eran presididas por el rey, eran siempre menos solemnes que las cortes' — 'they will demand it of you at a meeting or at court. The vistas, meetings arranged in advance, were sometimes judicial, like the district assemblies mentioned at 2014, 2949; though at times presided over by the king, they were always less solemn than the cortes.' retraer vos lo an, the future split by its pronouns: retraer + vos + lo + an (= os lo retraerán), 'they will reproach you with it'. Doña Sol's words foretell what comes. The speech ends here.

sentences.t: Lo que ruegan las dueñas non les ha ningún pro.
sentences.l: What beg the ladies not to-them has any profit.
sentences.i: What the ladies plead does them no good at all.
sentences.n: ruegan, 'they beg'. non … ningún, double negative. pro, 'profit, good': non les ha ningún pro, 'it is of no use to them' (ha, aver used impersonally).

sentences.t:
Essora les conpieçan a dar ifantes de Carrión;
con las çinchas corredizas májanlas tan sin sabor;
sentences.l:
Then to-them they-begin to strike Infantes of Carrión;
with the girths running they-beat-them so without savour;
sentences.i: Then the Infantes of Carrión begin to lay into them; with the running girths they thrash them most cruelly;
sentences.n: Essora = entonces, 'then'. conpieçan = comienzan. les … dar, 'to strike them' (dar, 'to deal blows'). corredizas, 'running, slipping', of girths: most simply the straps' loose running ends; the exact sense is not certain, and Pidal gives no note. májanlas = las majan, 'they beat them' (cf. majadas, v. 2732). tan sin sabor, literally 'so without savour, with no pleasure in it', taken here as 'so cruelly'; sabor comes back in the next line in the ladies' pain (mal sabor).

sentences.t:
con las espuelas agudas, don ellas an mal sabor,
ronpien las camisas e las carnes a ellas amas a dos:
linpia salie la sangre sobre los çiclatones.
Ya lo sienten ellas en los sos coraçones.
sentences.l:
with the spurs sharp, whence they have ill savour,
they-were-tearing the shifts and the flesh to them both two:
clean came-out the blood over the ciclatons.
Now it feel they in the their hearts.
sentences.i: with the sharp spurs, that hurt them cruelly, they tore the shifts and the flesh of both of them: the bright blood ran out over the silken tunics. Now they feel it in their very hearts.
sentences.n: don = donde, 'from which', of the spurs. an mal sabor, 'they have bitter pain' (an = han). ronpien = rompían, imperfect, 'they were tearing'. a ellas amas a dos, 'to them, both of the two'. linpia, 'clean', of the blood: bright, fresh. salie = salía. çiclatones, the silk robes of v. 2721. los sos coraçones, article + possessive, 'their hearts'.

sentences.t:
¡Quál ventura serie esta, si ploguiesse al Criador,
que assomasse essora el Çid Campeador!
sentences.l:
What fortune would-be this, if it-pleased the Creator,
that should-appear then the Çid Campeador!
sentences.i: What good fortune it would be, if it pleased the Creator, that the Çid Campeador should appear just then!
sentences.n: The singer breaks in with his own wish. serie = sería, conditional. ploguiesse, imperfect subjunctive of plazer, 'if it should please'. assomasse, imperfect subjunctive of assomar, 'to come into sight, appear'. essora, 'then'. Pidal's note to v. 2752 marks v. 2753 as a repetition of these two lines.

sentences.t:
Tanto las majaron que sin cosimente son;
sangrientas en las camisas e todos los ciclatones.
sentences.l:
So-much them they-beat that without strength they-are;
bloody in the shifts and all the ciclatons.
sentences.i: They beat them so long that they have no strength left, their shifts and all their silken tunics soaked with blood.
sentences.n: majaron, 'they beat'. Pidal's note to v. 2743: 'sin cosimente, probablemente "sin fuerzas, agotadas"' — 'probably "without strength, exhausted"': Pidal's own 'probably', the word being rare. The second line has no verb: sangrientas, 'bloodied', agreeing with the ladies. ciclatones, here without the cedilla, as printed (çiclatones at vv. 2721, 2739).

sentences.t:
Canssados son de ferir ellos amos a dos,
ensayandos amos quál dará mejores colpes.
sentences.l:
Tired are of striking they both two,
trying-themselves both which will-give better blows.
sentences.i: The two of them are worn out with striking, each vying with the other to deal the harder blows.
sentences.n: Canssados son de ferir, 'they are tired of striking' (ferir = herir, f- for h-). amos a dos, 'both of the two'. Pidal's note to v. 2746: 'esforzándose (v. 2388) ambos sobre quién golpeará mejor' — 'both exerting themselves over which would strike better'. ensayandos = ensayándose, the se cut to s; ensayarse, 'to exert oneself' (as at v. 2388). dará, future, 'will give'. colpes = golpes, giving the ó-e.

sentences.t:
Ya non pueden fablar don Elvira e doña Sol,
por muertas las dexaron en el robredo de Corpes.
sentences.l:
Now not can speak don Elvira and doña Sol,
for dead them they-left in the oak-wood of Corpes.
sentences.i: Doña Elvira and Doña Sol can speak no longer; for dead they left them in the oak wood of Corpes.
sentences.n: Ya non, 'no longer'. por muertas, 'for dead': las dexaron, 'they left them'. The line is said again in the next tirada, in its last line but one (v. 2752), and at the head of the one after (v. 2754-5), as Pidal's notes point out.

sentences.t:
Leváronles los mantos e las pieles armiñas,
mas déxanlas marridas en briales y en camisas,
e a las aves del monte e a las bestias de la fiera guisa.
sentences.l:
They-took-from-them the mantles and the furs ermine,
but they-leave-them fainting in tunics and in shifts,
and to the birds of-the wood and to the beasts of the fierce kind.
sentences.i: They took away their mantles and their ermine furs, and left them swooning in their tunics and their shifts, to the birds of the forest and the savage beasts.
sentences.n: Tirada 129 (assonance í-a) — the Infantes abandon their wives (a twin series) (Pidal: Los infantes abandonan a sus mujeres. (Serie gemela.)). The line-ends run armiñas, camisas, guisa, bivas, Díaz: í with a after it. A twin series tells the same moment over again in a new assonance; Pidal's note to v. 2752 calls 2749–50 like 2720–21. Leváronles = les llevaron, 'they took from them'. pieles armiñas, 'ermine furs', armiñas an adjective. Pidal's note to v. 2750: 'marrido, generalmente significa "afligido, apenado"; aquí "desmayado"' — 'marrido generally means "afflicted, grieved"; here "fainting"'. briales, 'tunics', the close-fitting robe Pidal equates with the ciclatón (note to v. 2721). de la fiera guisa, 'of the fierce sort', savage. The tense moves from Leváronles to déxanlas.

sentences.t:
Por muertas la[s] dexaron, sabed, que non por bivas.
¡Quál ventura serie si assomas essora el Çid [Roy Díaz]!
sentences.l:
For dead them they-left, know-ye, and not for alive.
What fortune would-be if should-appear then the Çid [Roy Díaz]!
sentences.i: They left them for dead, be sure of it, and not for living. What good fortune it would be if the Çid, Ruy Díaz, were to appear just then!
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 2752: 'Repetición de 2748. Al tono lírico de este pasaje convienen las repeticiones; así 2749-50 son semejantes a 2720-21, y 2753 es semejante a 2741-42. Véanse además las notas a 2754 y 2763' — 'A repetition of 2748. Repetition suits the lyric tone of this passage: so 2749–50 are like 2720–21, and 2753 is like 2741–42. See also the notes to 2754 and 2763.' la[s], the s Pidal's. sabed, 'know (it)', the singer to his hearers. que non por bivas, 'and not for living'. assomas = assomasse, imperfect subjunctive 3rd sg., the final -e dropped and the stress left on the a (assomás, though printed without an accent), as fincás at v. 2709; it echoes que assomasse at v. 2742. [Roy Díaz], both words Pidal's restoration (in italics), which gives the line its í-a ending: Ruy Díaz, the Çid's own name.

sentences.t:
Ifantes de Carrión por muertas las dexaron,
que el una al otra nol torna recabdo.
sentences.l:
Infantes of Carrión for dead them they-left,
that the one to-the other not-to-her returns heed.
sentences.i: The Infantes of Carrión left them for dead, so that neither could do anything for the other.
sentences.n: Tirada 130 (assonance á-o) — the Infantes boast of their cowardice (Pidal: Los infantes se alaban de su cobardía). The line-ends run dexaron, recabdo, alabando, vengados, rogados, braços, vengando: á with o after it. Pidal numbers the first line 2754-5: one line bearing two numbers, kept as printed. Pidal's note to v. 2754: 'Verso de encadenamiento, semejante al penúltimo de la serie anterior, y tercera repetición de 2748' — 'a linking line, like the last but one of the previous series, and the third repetition of 2748'. el una al otra, 'the one to the other', el before a feminine word beginning with a vowel. nol = non + le, le the dative 'to her', taking up al otra. torna recabdo, literally 'returns heed', i.e. attends, answers: recabdo, 'care, heed'; the sense 'neither could tend to or answer the other' is taken from context, Pidal giving no note.

sentences.t:
Por los montes do ivan, ellos ívanse alabando:
“De nuestros casamientos agora somos vengados.
sentences.l:
Through the woods where they-were-going, they were-going-themselves praising:
“Of our marriages now we-are avenged.
sentences.i: Through the woods as they went, they went boasting: “Now we are avenged for our marriages.
sentences.n: do = donde. ívanse alabando, ir + gerund, 'they went boasting' (alabarse, 'to boast'). agora = ahora. somos vengados, 'we are avenged': the marriages themselves are the wrong they count as avenged.

sentences.t:
Non las deviemos tomar por varraganas, si non f[o]ssemos rogados,
pues nuestras parejas non eran pora en braços.
La desondra del león assís irá vengando.”
sentences.l:
Not them we-ought to-take for concubines, if not we-were begged,
since our equals not they-were for in arms.
The dishonour of-the lion thus-itself will-go avenging.”
sentences.i: We should not have taken them even as concubines unless we had been begged to, for they were not our equals, fit to be wives in our arms. Thus shall the dishonour of the lion be avenged.”
sentences.n: Pidal numbers this long line 2759-60: one line with two numbers, kept as printed; its last word, rogados, runs over in the print to the end of the next line. deviemos = debíamos, imperfect indicative 1st pl. with the old ending -iemos (= -íamos), used of what ought to have been: non las deviemos tomar, 'we ought not to have taken them'. varraganas = barraganas, 'concubines' — not to be confused with barragán, 'valiant man', said of Avengalvón at v. 2671. si non f[o]ssemos rogados, 'unless we had been begged', fuéssemos with the o Pidal's. Pidal's note to v. 2759-60: 'Los infantes creían que aun para tomar a las hijas del Cid por barraganas debían haber sido instados por un rogador (v. 2080); comp. 3276' — 'the Infantes held that even to take the Çid's daughters as concubines they ought to have been urged to it by a go-between' (rogador, 'asker, intercessor': at vv. 2079–2080 the king bade all present join in asking for the brides). Pidal's note to v. 2761: '"pues no eran iguales nuestras para ser nuestras mujeres legítimas". Pareja se había hecho sustantivo, significando "mujer legítima", 3277, y también se dice pareja pora en braços, 3449; comp. 255, 2333' — 'for they were not our equals, to be our lawful wives. Pareja had become a noun meaning "lawful wife"'. pora = para. assís = assí + se, the se making the line passive: assís irá vengando, 'thus will it go being avenged', ir + gerund of a thing done step by step, future: the shame of the lion is being paid off and will be (cf. v. 2719). The speech, and the part, end here.
